title: Coordinate description of the maximal branch stratum
statement: Let $U$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ be regular functions on $U$, with $s\geq 1$. Suppose that for every point $u\in U$, the germs of exactly those $t_j$ vanishing at $u$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$; a regular system of parameters of a regular local ring of dimension $d$ means $d$ generators of its maximal ideal. Put $D_U=V(\prod_{j=1}^s t_j)$ and $C=V(t_1,\ldots,t_s)$, as closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $b(\bar u)=\#\{j:t_j(u)=0\text{ in }\kappa(u)\}$. This is the number of geometric local branches of $D_U$, equivalently the number of minimal primes of the reduced strict henselian local ring of $D_U$ at $\bar u$, with branch number zero off $D_U$. It is unchanged on passing to an etale neighborhood [def-weil-etale-morphism] and is independent of a choice of such coordinate equations. For every integer $k$, the subset $\{b\geq k\}$ is the union of the coordinate intersections $V(t_j:j\in J)$ with $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and $|J|=k$ (all of $U$ for $k\leq0$, empty for $k>s$). In particular $b\leq s$, and $b=s$ exactly on $C$. The closed subscheme $C$ is regular and reduced, and is permitted to be empty; the value $s$ is attained if and only if $C$ is nonempty. The same assertions hold after every etale base change. Here the reduced strict henselian local ring at a geometric point is the reduction of the filtered colimit of local rings of its pointed etale neighborhoods, and a minimal prime is a prime ideal minimal under inclusion.

proof.text: Fix $u$ and let $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, a regular local ring by [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $I=\{j:t_j(u)=0\}$. Factors outside $I$ are units, so $\mathcal O_{D_U,u}=A/(F)$ for $F=\prod_{j\in I}t_j$ when $I\neq\varnothing$. For $\bar u$ over $u\in D_U$, apply [lem-sbc-geometric-strict-henselization-local-presentation] on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq D_U$ containing $u$: it gives a prime $q\subset R$ such that the geometric strict local ring $H$ of $D_U$ at $\bar u$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $R_q$ relative to a separable closure of its residue field, compatibly with $R\to H$. The prime $q$ is that of $u$: $R_q\to H$ is local, so $q$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak m_H$, which is the kernel of the residue map $R\to\Omega$ induced by $\bar u$. Hence $R_q=A/(F)$ and $H$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $A/(F)$ for the residue-field choice selected by $\bar u$. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-product-strict-local-branches] to the distinct parameter germs indexed by $I$: its reduction has exactly $|I|$ minimal primes. If $I=\varnothing$, $u\notin D_U$ and the count is zero. This identifies $b$ intrinsically and proves independence of coordinate equations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-intersection-geometry] with $J=\{1,\ldots,s\}$ to obtain that $C$ is regular and reduced, allowing $C=\varnothing$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given regularity, local Noetherianity and pointwise parameter condition.

proof.text: For $1\le k\le s$, the finite set $I_u$ has at least $k$ elements if and only if it contains a subset $J$ of cardinality $k$. For that $J$, every $t_j$, $j\in J$, has zero residue at $u$, which is exactly membership in $V(t_j:j\in J)$ by the closed-subscheme equations [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves the asserted union formula. For $k\le0$ the inequality holds at every point; for $k>s$ it holds nowhere. There are only finitely many subsets $J$, so each nontrivial union is closed. Taking $k=s$ gives $b=s$ exactly on the underlying set of $C$, and $0\le b\le s$ follows from $I_u\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$. Therefore $s$ occurs if and only if $C$ has a point; a geometric point above any such point is obtained by taking an algebraic closure of its residue field.

proof.text: For any etale $e:W\to U$, [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-intersection-geometry] gives a regular locally Noetherian $W$, the coordinate hypothesis for $e^*t_j$, and identical vanishing-index sets at $w$ and $e(w)$. Apply Steps 1--3 to these functions on $W$; these steps have already proved the assertions on every chart satisfying that hypothesis. Pullback of the equations gives $D_W=V(\prod e^*t_j)$ and $C_W=V(e^*t_1,\ldots,e^*t_s)$. Hence every assertion holds on $W$, and the equal index sets give $b_W(\bar w)=b_U(\bar u)$. Applying the intrinsic formula also to any alternative coordinate equations for the same $D_W$ proves their branch counts agree.
